genZNote: The classic hand-foot-and-mouth disease virus of daycare outbreaks — small, hardy, and extremely good at spreading among kids.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human gastrointestinal tract, with secondary spread to skin/mucosa and occasionally heart/CNS
habitat.hostAssociation: Humans are the sole natural host and reservoir
habitat.reservoir: Infected humans, particularly children in daycare/school settings

culture.growthCharacteristics: Can be cultured in specific cell lines; PCR of vesicle fluid, throat, or stool is now the standard diagnostic method

identificationClues: Classic cause of hand-foot-and-mouth disease — vesicular lesions on the palms, soles, and oral mucosa, typically in young children
Also causes herpangina (painful vesicles/ulcers on the posterior oropharynx) and, less commonly, viral (aseptic) meningitis and myopericarditis
Non-enveloped RNA virus, environmentally hardy and resistant to alcohol-based hand sanitizers, spreading efficiently via the fecal-oral route and respiratory droplets/vesicle fluid
A member of the enterovirus genus, related to poliovirus and other picornaviruses

clinicalImportance.transmission: Fecal-oral route, respiratory droplets, and contact with vesicle fluid; highly contagious in daycare/school settings
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: One of the most common causes of childhood exanthems worldwide, with seasonal peaks in summer and fall in temperate climates
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: PCR of vesicle fluid, throat swab, or stool is now the standard diagnostic approach, having largely replaced viral culture

examFacts.importantTest: PCR of vesicle fluid, throat swab, or stool
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Classic non-enveloped enterovirus behind hand-foot-and-mouth disease, a hallmark pediatric exanthem
